comparator.name: English Language and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA study-programme page accounts for the complete 180-EC English Language and Culture bachelor. Year 1 comprises ten compulsory 6-EC courses across English linguistics, literature, theory, rhetoric and writing, textual research and linguistic research methods. Year 2 contains three named compulsory literature/research courses (18 EC), 18 EC of restricted-choice core, 12 EC of programme-related electives and 12 EC of free choice. Year 3 contains Philosophy of the Humanities, Debates in English Studies, English Research Seminar, 30 EC of free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The normalized target is generic and the official programme offers World Literatures in English or English Linguistics and Literature in years 2 and 3. English Linguistics and Literature most broadly preserves the programme title’s combined language-and-literature identity, so it is selected under the neutral broad-academic-identity rule before UCR course selection. The route is instantiated with the official linguistics-side restricted-choice core options, English Linguistics 5: Language in Society (12 EC) and English Linguistics 6: The Changing English Language (6 EC); genuine programme-related and free-choice space remains explicit rather than being filled with invented electives.

candidates.label: World literatures in English, textual interpretation and cultural power

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the general English Language and Culture bachelor rather than one specialisation. Of the two official specialisations, English Linguistics and Literature most broadly preserves the programme title’s combined language-and-literature identity, while World Literatures in English is the more specialised literature route. The combined route is selected independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match is complemented by two feasible generator-backed directions: world literatures with textual interpretation and cultural power, and English with identity and global culture. Each produces a materially different curriculum and exceeds the pairwise 30-EC/four-course distinctness floor, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

alternatives.label: English literature, culture & language
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum balances English-language literature and cultural analysis with language, communication, sociolinguistic context and independent research.
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible response to English Language and Culture combining literary study, rhetoric, communication and textual interpretation with historical, social, political, media and psycholinguistic perspectives on English-speaking cultures.
progression: Introductory literature, rhetoric, brain and behaviour, history, sociology, media and politics precede advanced literary, cultural, communication and psycholinguistic work. Research Methods & Statistics and qualitative methods precede advanced historical and literary research. All prerequisites and planned-semester constraints are satisfied.

alternatives.label: Literature, media & transforming texts
alternatives.labelReason: The route is organised around literary interpretation, film, media, adaptation, art, cultural theory and creative production, directly reflecting the two literature-led specialisations.
alternatives.concept: A literature-and-media route combining literary interpretation, film, media history, adaptation, documentary, rhetoric and creative communication with social and historical context.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces politics, international relations, psycholinguistics and advanced history with media archaeology, environmental media, documentary, advanced art-historical methods and a denser sequence in literary and visual transformation. Eight of 24 courses differ, a 60-EC change.
progression: Introductory literature, film and media, rhetoric, history, art history, sociology and research methods precede literary theory, adaptation, documentary, race and media, creative communication and art-historical research. All prerequisites and planned-semester constraints are satisfied.

alternatives.label: English, identity & global culture
alternatives.labelReason: The route foregrounds language, identity, social belonging and global cultural circulation through communication, sociology, media, history, politics and psycholinguistics.
alternatives.concept: A global-English and identity route combining literature and communication with sociology, history, politics, media, social identity, cultural memory and psycholinguistic perspectives.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces four literature, art and international-relations courses with environmental media, advanced social theory, Native American history and a focused social-identity psychology course. Compared with the literature-and-media route, eight courses differ. The organising emphasis is social variation, identity and global cultural life.
progression: Foundations in communication, sociology, literature, media, modern history and politics precede advanced social theory, identity and media, Indigenous history, creative communication and psycholinguistics. Qualitative and statistical foundations precede advanced research. All prerequisites and planned-semester constraints are satisfied.

notes.text: The UvA programme provides a specialist sequence in English literary history, English linguistics and World Englishes, with route-specific core choice, a research seminar and a dedicated English Language and Culture thesis. UCR can build coherent literature/culture/language, literature/media and English/identity/global-culture pathways, but it does not reproduce the full English phonology, morphology, grammar, sociolinguistics and period-literature sequence or the dedicated English thesis structure.
